paper.title: StableMimic: Smooth Human-Like Recovery for Humanoid Motion Tracking - Learning Beyond the Tracking Distribution for Structured Post-Fall Behavior
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-08-03; retrieved 2026-08-30; PDF SHA-256 a682d048fdd10fc16671b7af3bca82414fb70652f039e7fa788b343b0beb86d0; source SHA-256 dec60ed8b8aaff149e33c162eea9742d67681f9cdc68978114a2b2910032c07f

decision_relevance.why_admitted: It gives a source-located design for selecting and advancing hidden recovery references, shaping physical successor states, and handing control back to an advancing command, plus an independent post-fall evaluation protocol. Its multi-component intervention makes the fixed-trainer boundary unusually important.
not_evidence_for: A reward-only or oracle-only improvement under Sam's fixed trainer
A natural-language or LLM-driven policy-training harness
An external OGMP state machine or predicate-branching oracle
Formal reachability outside sampled recovery support
Causal independence of the two Actor experts
Compatibility with an arbitrary frozen foundation controller

mechanisms.name: Training-only recovery-reference oracle
mechanisms.description: A sequence-disjoint get-up library supplies a sampled trajectory and frame, a perturbed reset neighborhood, a hidden advancing reference, and failure-adaptive frame resampling; reference identity and phase are never exposed to the deployed Actor.

mechanisms.name: Hidden successor-state recovery reward
mechanisms.description: During recovery, the physical successor state is compared with the next hidden get-up state using six Gaussian-kernel error families; the live command remains visible but contributes no tracking reference term until transition.

mechanisms.name: Reference reacquisition and realignment
mechanisms.description: Terminal recovery similarity initiates a 1.5-second transition to the continuously advancing command; horizontal translation is aligned to the recovered pose while command yaw and local motion continuity are retained.

mechanisms.name: Proprioception-gated dual-expert Actor
mechanisms.description: Commanded-motion and recovery experts receive the same deployable command-conditioned history; a proprioception-only soft gate blends their action means continuously and is trained with privileged regime labels.

mechanisms.name: Asymmetric training/deployment boundary
mechanisms.description: Training-only get-up features and simulator state enter reset/reward logic and the privileged Critic, while deployed Actor get-up slots remain permanently zero and routing uses only proprioceptive history.

mechanisms.name: Load-aware recovery regularization
mechanisms.description: Action-rate, joint-limit, self-collision, and power penalties discourage aggressive correction during recovery but are explicitly not a safety certification.

failure_modes.name: Recovery-support boundary
failure_modes.description: The perturbed neighborhoods around get-up trajectories are empirical supports, not formal reachability sets; states beyond them are outside the paper's claim.

failure_modes.name: Load-aware is not safety-certified
failure_modes.description: Regularizers and post-fall load metrics support bounded behavior only under the evaluated protocol; they do not certify safety.

failure_modes.name: Two-knob identification gap
failure_modes.description: The main system jointly changes references, reset distribution, reward, Actor/Critic architecture, and auxiliary losses; it does not identify the gain from reference composition or task reward alone under a frozen trainer.

failure_modes.name: Non-uniform baseline training and command interfaces
failure_modes.description: Full-system baselines retain their original training procedures and receive different native command interfaces, so cross-method rankings are protocol evidence rather than an isolated causal comparison.

failure_modes.name: Descriptive MoE dynamics
failure_modes.description: Earlier curve stabilization and lower policy standard deviation are explicitly descriptive, not causal evidence of expert independence.

failure_modes.name: Qualitative hardware evidence
failure_modes.description: Real-G1 dance and standing recoveries are qualitative demonstrations, not a matched hardware architecture comparison or quantitative reliability estimate.

evaluation.name: Complete LAFAN1 dance tracking
evaluation.description: On the complete retargeted LAFAN1 dance subset, StableMimic reports MPBPE 28.53 mm, MJAE 88.83e-3 rad, MJAVE 798.22e-3 rad/s, and relative acceleration error 2.08 mm/frame^2, the lowest values among five methods in Table III.

evaluation.name: Matched push-to-fall recovery
evaluation.description: Across 100 shared disturbances, StableMimic reports 100/100 recovery, limb-speed P95 4.91 m/s, limb path 13.80 m, joint-speed P95 5.26 rad/s, target-rate P95 17.35 rad/s, displacement 1.32 m, torque P95 19.64 N m, and positive energy 0.61 kJ; it is lowest on six of seven motion/load measures, while BFM-Zero has lower target rate.

evaluation.name: Controlled Single-MLP architecture ablation
evaluation.description: With common observations, actions, Critic, reward, and PPO, the larger Single-MLP Actor reports 32.66 mm MPBPE and 98/100 recovery versus 28.53 mm and 100/100 for the MoE; this isolates architecture more closely than it isolates the reference or reward mechanisms.

evaluation.name: Real-G1 qualitative deployment
evaluation.description: Separate dance and constant-standing ONNX Actors run at 50 Hz and qualitatively recover after induced falls before resuming their commands; no matched hardware statistics are reported.

evidence.locator: Versioned metadata and abstract; submitted 3 Aug 2026; arXiv comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, preprint not formally peer reviewed
evidence.claim: arXiv v1 fixes the title, authors, public date, abstract-level contributions, and preprint status.

evidence.locator: Section III-A, Equation (1), Figure 2, and Table II
evidence.claim: The Actor has four-frame deployable history and permanently zeroed get-up slots; recovery references and privileged state are confined to training-only reset/reward/Critic paths.
A sampled perturbed get-up frame initializes recovery, the hidden reference advances, and the physical successor is scored against the next hidden reference state.

evidence.locator: Section III-B, paragraphs after Equation (2), and Figure 4
evidence.claim: Failure-adaptive frame sampling, a 2-second error tolerance, and a 1.5-second transition structure the recovery-to-command lifecycle; coverage beyond sampled support is excluded.

evidence.locator: Section III-C, Equation (3), Auxiliary gate supervision
evidence.claim: A proprioception-only soft gate continuously blends commanded-motion and recovery expert means and receives training-only regime supervision.

Regime-conditioned reference reward uses six Gaussian-kernel error families, translated recovery uses root height, the recovery coefficient is 2.5 times nominal, and load-aware regularizers do not certify safety.

evidence.locator: Section III-D, deployment and reference-alignment paragraphs
evidence.claim: Deployment removes the get-up library and hard switch; horizontal translation is realigned to the recovered pose while command yaw and local continuity remain.

evidence.locator: Section IV-A, Tasks and protocols and Comparison methods
evidence.claim: The paper evaluates sequence-disjoint LAFAN1 tracking/get-up subsets on nominal MuJoCo G1 and uses 100 matched pushes; full-system baselines retain native training and command interfaces.
Tracking metrics, fall thresholds, recovery denominator, and three-second post-fall motion/control/load metrics are explicitly defined.
StableMimic reports 28.53 mm MPBPE, 88.83e-3 rad MJAE, 798.22e-3 rad/s MJAVE, and 2.08 mm/frame^2 relative acceleration error, the lowest table values among five methods.
StableMimic reports 100/100 recovery and the lowest six of seven post-fall motion/load measures under the matched disturbance protocol.

evidence.locator: Section IV-C, Analysis of the MoE Design
evidence.claim: Training curves are described as consistent with reduced interference but explicitly not causal evidence of expert independence.

evidence.locator: Section IV-D, Main Hardware Results and Scope
evidence.claim: Dance and standing policies qualitatively recover on a real G1; the authors state this is not safety certification or a matched hardware architecture comparison.
The paper tabulates exact network, PPO, gate-loss, training, and recovery-reset settings.
